title: Initiative ownership matrix and quarterly release cadence for company OKR alignment
creator: Leah Park
description:
Problem statement: As Redwood scales, company-level OKRs are drifting between strategic intent and execution because initiative ownership boundaries, release cadences, and handoff criteria are inconsistent across teams. This causes duplicate work, missed dependencies (especially between Dedicated and Private), and reactive re-prioritization during the quarter.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, repeatable playbook that maps company OKRs to a) a clear initiative ownership matrix and b) a synchronized quarterly release cadence with explicit gating criteria. The playbook should be operational (checklists, templates) and integrated with our PM/Eng/Design workflows (Linear, GitHub Projects, Console dashboards).

Scope: 
- Company-level OKRs -> canonical initiative list and owners (RACI-lite)
- Initiative ownership matrix (primary owner, cross-functional leads, escalation owner)
- Quarterly release cadence with milestones, sync points, and decision gates (planning, canary, launch, post-mortem)
- Templates for initiative-level PRD + rollout checklist + dependency registration form
- Integration points: Linear project templates, GitHub board labels, Notion playbook, Console KPI dashboards to measure OKR progress

Out of scope: Team-level sprint cadence definitions, tooling implementation (automation will be follow-up).

Success metrics: 
- 90% of company initiatives have an assigned primary owner and at least one cross-functional lead by Q2 planning kickoff
- <2 untracked cross-team dependencies discovered after planning cut (goal: zero)
- 1st cycle adoption: runbook used by >=80% of product initiatives during Q2 planning

Trade-offs and decisions so far: 
- Lightweight over prescriptive: we opt for RACI-lite (Primary / Support / Escalation) instead of full RACI to reduce friction.
- Synchronous cadence cadence: prefer a fixed quarterly backbone with monthly health syncs rather than weekly heavy meetings.
- Tooling: start with docs and Linear templates, defer automation/integrations to a follow-up sprint (dependency on ENG-2671).

Deliverables (iteration 1): 
1) Notion playbook with ownership matrix template and release cadence checklist (link below).
2) Linear project template and issue naming convention.
3) GitHub board label schema and example board for company initiatives.
4) Example usage: map of Q2 company OKRs to initiatives + assigned owners (seed list).

Operational notes: 
- Ownership matrices must be updated by initiative owners during planning week; PMs to confirm ownership in the kickoff sync.
- Escalation path: owner -> product lead -> VP Product (Omar Patel) -> exec triage.

Risks: 
- If eng capacity estimates are inconsistent, the cadence may create false predictability. Mitigation: require a 2-point capacity buffer in the release checklist and a standard engineering estimate rubric.
- Overhead risk for small initiatives; mitigation: scale templates by initiative size and allow opt-outs (with approval).
